messages.author: 661599c031af2f3f
messages.subject: LGM baseline estimation failed?
parts:
Dear all,
we are fitting a substantial lgm (12 waves, N=25k). Model estimation proceeds normally, fit stats (e.g. chi sq=630, df=63, rmsea=0.022) and parameters look sensible. However, lavaan reports that the 'baseline model estimation has failed'. This is a bit inconvenient as it doesn't allow us to compute e.g. CFI to report. I have tried the same model in e.g. Onyx to see whether it was our data/model but I could reproduce the fit/parameter estimates exactly for the hypothesized model, and the baseline model converged fine ion onyx. One might be inclined to switch to onyx but that is slow to estimate for large models and cumbersome for multigroup models (despite its many other strengths), so I'd rather stick with lavaan. I also reproduced the same model in openmx which also computed a nullmodel just fine, but openmyx seems very sensitive to starting values and MLR/multigroup constraints (and general syntax) are much more inconvenient, so again I prefer lavaan if at all possible - Do you have any suggestions for us, or further information to share? Should we go back a few lavaan versions perhaps?

On 7/7/20 12:12 AM, Rogier Kievit wrote:
> Dear all,
> we are fitting a substantial lgm (12 waves, N=25k). Model estimation
> proceeds normally, fit stats (e.g. chi sq=630, df=63, rmsea=0.022) and
> parameters look sensible. However, lavaan reports that the 'baseline
> model estimation has failed'.

Hm. I am not sure. But this is not supposed to happen. I would like to
investigate this further. Is it possible to send me (Yves dot Rosseel at
UGent dot be) the script and the data? Or a snippet of the data, or
simulated data: as long as it triggers this warning.

Too 'see' what goes wrong, you can try this (assuming 'fit' is your
fitted model):

fit0 <- lavaan:::lav_object_independence(fit)

This will fit the baseline model, and report any warning/errors as usual.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: LGM baseline estimation failed?
parts:
Thanks for the reprex. That helped. This is now fixed in lavaan dev
0.6-7.1570, which you can install by typing in R:

install.packages("lavaan", repos = "https://www.da.ugent.be", type =
"source")

The cause was a 0% coverage for a pair of variables leading to a NA
value in the sample.cov matrix that is used to generate the starting
values of the baseline model.

Yves.
